newsitem.title: ITALY: Ambroveneto chief discounts takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: Ambroveneto chief discounts takeover talk.

text.p: The chairman of Italy's Banco Ambrosiano Veneto (Ambroveneto) Giovanni Bazoli said on Wednesday that he was not worried about rumours of takeover bids after the bank's shares had made huge gains on the Milan bourse.

"I don't see any possibility for an action like this because our share control syndicate gives members first rights of purchase and would therefore put an end to any such hypothesis," he said while attending a executive committee meeting of Italian banking association ABI.
Bazoli confirmed that savings bank Cassa di Risparmio di Verona (CariVerona) had decided to sell its 12.5 percent stake in Ambroveneto.
He said members of the Ambroveneto shareholders' syndicate, which retains a 69.5 percent holding in the bank, would now decide on the future of the CariVerona stake.
Shares held by the syndicate can be sold to a third party.
Ambroveneto is planning a merger with Milan-based savings bank Cariplo and the market in many banking shares has been boosted by talk of takeovers and restructuring.

Shares in Ambroveneto rose nearly 10 percent on both Monday and Tuesday this week, and were up nearly 10 percent on Wednesday before Bazoli's comments pushed them lower. At 1110 GMT, the shares were off 5.92 percent at 7,580 lire.
